text:
Jason Robertson's future is the story around him, more than his play. Over the last two weeks the headlines have been about an extension Dallas wants and an insider who doubts he signs long term, plus one floated blockbuster with Nikita Kucherov. None of that has come from Robertson or the Stars.

On the ice he's fine. He has 24 points in 21 games, a hat trick against Washington on Nov. 3, and two assists in Tuesday's comeback in Vegas. His own goals run only a little hot, 10 on 8.0 expected. The padding is on-ice: Dallas has scored 7.7 more goals than the chances deserve with him out there, which flatters his assist total. His shot generation is also down from last season, 1.18 expected goals per 60 after 1.37.

Last season Evolving-Hockey had him 14th of 401 forwards at 3.1 wins above replacement, driving play at the 98th percentile, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking put him in the 90th percentile for chances from the slot area. That's the player Dallas would be paying for. We'd watch whether his shot rate climbs back.
